Product and architecture

Serve a dated JSON snapshot first. Let the browser request current data where upstream CORS permits. Keep immutable snapshots, provenance and source licences in the repository. Precompute indexes and graphs for predictable loading.

Upstream sourcesOWASP public JSON, GitHub, Wikimedia
Collection workflowCapture, validate, preserve evidence
Versioned repositorySnapshots, graph, index, provenance
Browser experienceDirectory, graph, archive, live fetch

What is working here

  • Search and filter 347 captured projects.
  • Inspect explicit project relationships in a navigable graph.
  • Search 7,265 archived wiki titles, plus the two captured page bodies.
  • Load live project JSON and archive pages directly in the browser, subject to upstream access.
  • Download a source package with Python collectors and a proposed daily GitHub Actions workflow.

Freshness and history

Record capture time, source update time and the last successful check independently. Keep a stable identity map between old wiki paths, GitHub website repositories and current slugs. A recovered document’s source date is distinct from today’s retrieval date.

Decisions for the implementing agent

  • Choose the destination repository and confirm source-specific republication terms.
  • Connect the collector and review the proposed 06:00 UTC daily schedule.
  • Expand full-text historical coverage and map old pages to current projects.
  • Check source schema changes, missing classifications, expired media and error recovery.
  • Map each demonstrated behaviour to the team’s actual RiskMandate policy definition and version.

RiskMandate demonstration

Record the requested action, policy ID and version, decision, supporting evidence, any approval and the action taken. Demonstrate a successful run, conflicting records and a retry. Policy mapping and enforcement remain implementation work.

Conversation context

Readiness and scope

This private research site supports review of captured public source material. Automated collection is inactive until a destination repository is connected. The current OWASP API’s stability and reuse terms, historical archive completeness and full original-page rendering remain open verification items.

    PROVIDER ACCESS REVIEW

    Can the browser access Spotify?

    Yes, for supported user data after Spotify authorisation. OAuth permissions, app quotas and platform terms determine access.

    Research reviewed 22 November 2026

    Account access has not been exercised. This page documents the supported integration route and its limits.

    Supported routes

    RouteWhat it offersDependency
    Browser Web APISupported profile, playlist, library and recent-play endpointsRegistered Spotify app, exact redirect URI, user consent and OAuth with PKCE
    MCP connectorAgent-facing tools over a provider integrationConnector capabilities, its authentication and upstream permissions
    Account data exportJSON packages, including extended streaming historyUser requests and supplies the selected export

    An MCP connector and a browser client can expose different capabilities. Each still needs the upstream authentication and permissions. A signed-in Spotify tab alone does not authorise another site’s JavaScript to read private data.

    Authentication and deployment constraints

    Spotify recommends PKCE for browser apps. Request minimum scopes and keep client secrets out of frontend code. Development mode currently requires a Premium app owner and supports up to five allowlisted users. Developer-account quotas are shared across development apps.

    Historical data

    The recently played endpoint is a bounded recent-history feed. Spotify’s extended streaming history export is documented as covering the account lifetime. The export can contain identifiers and network information, so select the files and fields needed for the intended private feature.

    Reuse and agent limits

    Spotify’s Developer Policy restricts content analysis, recreating its core experience, standalone metadata services and ingestion of Spotify Content into AI models. The noncommercial purpose of this project still requires compliance with those terms. Confirm the exact feature and any required permission before applying the OWASP archive or graph approach to Spotify data.

    A useful first technical proof would display supported account data in a private, authorised browser app and document the fields and scopes. An agent can help implement the app using developer documentation. Any processing of retrieved Spotify Content by an AI model needs separate review against the policy.

    Connector availability

    No Spotify plugin was returned by the plugin search available in this session. Other directories and independently hosted MCP servers may offer integrations. Their presence alone does not establish Spotify endorsement or additional data rights.
